function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a convenient online option. | Category | What to Look For | Why It Might Be Right for You | |----------|------------------|------------------------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • Small‑batch, artisanal cakes
• Custom designs & seasonal flavors
• Often use fresh, locally sourced ingredients | Great for unique flavor profiles, supporting small businesses, and getting a personalized touch. | | **National Chains** | • Costco, Walmart, Target, Trader Joe’s, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Aldi, etc.
• Standardized menu items (e.g., chocolate, vanilla, red velvet)
• Usually have a “cake” section in the bakery aisle | Convenient, often cheaper, and you can pick up in-store or order online for delivery. | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | • Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, Instacart, Shipt, Amazon Fresh, Walmart Grocery, Target Same‑Day Delivery | These apps let you browse multiple bakeries at once, compare prices, see real‑time delivery windows, and read customer reviews. | | **Specialty Cake Shops** | • Goldbelly (for gourmet cakes shipped nationwide)
• Cake Boss, Magnolia Bakery, Baked by Melissa, Sprinkles, Sweet Lady Jane, etc.
• Offer custom orders, themed cakes, and premium ingredients | Ideal if you want a show‑stopping centerpiece, custom decorations, or a cake that’s a bit out of the ordinary. | | **Grocery Stores with Online Ordering** | • Whole Foods, Wegmans, H-E-B, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, etc.
• Many now offer same‑day delivery via their own app or through Instacart/Shipt | Good balance between convenience and quality; many have a dedicated bakery section. | | **Specialty Dietary Options** | • Gluten‑free, vegan, keto, dairy‑free, nut‑free, sugar‑free, etc.
• Check labels or ask the baker directly | Essential if you or your guests have allergies or dietary restrictions. | ### How to Choose the Best Option 1. **Know Your Needs** * **Size & Shape** – Do you need a tiered wedding cake, a single‑layer birthday cake, or a novelty shape? * **Flavor & Theme** – Classic vanilla, decadent chocolate, exotic fruit, or a custom design? * **Dietary Restrictions** – Gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free, etc.? 2. **Check Reviews & Ratings** * On Google Maps, Yelp, or the platform’s own rating system. * Look for photos of previous cakes to gauge quality and creativity. 3. **Delivery Time & Availability** * Some platforms offer “same‑day” or “next‑day” delivery windows. * Local bakeries may have limited hours but can guarantee freshness. 4. **Price Range** * Local artisan cakes tend to be pricier ($30–$100+ depending on size). * National chain cakes are usually $10–$25. * Specialty shops or online gourmet sites can range from $50 to several hundred dollars. 5. **Contact Directly When Needed** * If you’re ordering a custom design or have special dietary questions, call or email the bakery. * Most local shops appreciate a phone call to confirm details. ### Quick Order Checklist | Step | Action | Tips | |------|--------|------| | 1 | Decide on the occasion (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.). | Helps narrow down cake size and style. | | 2 | Pick a delivery method (in‑store pickup vs. home delivery). | Pickup saves on delivery fees. | | 3 | Browse at least three options (local, chain, online). | Compare prices, reviews, and delivery times. | | 4 | Place your order early (especially for custom cakes). | Gives bakers time to prepare and ship. | | 5 | Confirm delivery address, time window, and payment method. | Avoid last‑minute surprises. | --- #### Want More Specific Recommendations? If you tell me your city or ZIP code, I can pull up a curated list of top-rated bakeries and delivery options in your area, complete with links, phone numbers, and average delivery times. Feel free to share that info, and I’ll dig deeper!
